newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Peptide sees U.K. listing, 95/96 loss.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Peptide sees U.K. listing, 95/96 loss.

text.p: Drug development firm Peptide Technology Ltd said on Wednesday it had revived plans to achieve a London Stock Exchange listing by early March 1997, accompanied by a 10 million pounds sterling capital raising.

The company, which told shareholders in late September that it had postponed its London listing plans due to poor market conditions, said its new float plans would include the presentation of a new set of financial accounts to investors.
Peptide executive director operations, Darryl Mellish, also told Reuters the company was due to report another loss for the 1995/96 year ended September 30.

"We have been doing a lot of research and development so a modest loss is likely," Mellish said. Peptide incurred a net loss of A$50.5 million in 1994/95 due to an accounting change in which research and development is immediately written-off.
Mellish said Peptide would probably seek lead investors for its London share issue and was not sure that it would continue with Nomura as the placing agent.

The company has shareholder approval to raise new capital until March 3 next year but has to compile a fresh set of audited accounts because it did not achieve a London listing by September 30, 1996, its balance date.
Peptide said in a statement that Paul Hookway had resigned as chairman but would remain a director.
It said he had been replaced by Tony Bates who would work with management to achieve a London listing.
Bates was formerly managing director of Cyanamid Australia and New Zealand.
